visual.general_description: Two side-by-side grayscale axial abdominal CT images (A and B) at the level of the upper liver, showing a rounded mass in the posterior right hepatic lobe in two contrast phases.
visual.detailed_description: Panel A, labelled A at upper left: axial CT slice with the liver on the left of the image and the spleen on the right. A rounded mass lies in the posterior part of the liver near the lateral margin and looks brighter and more heterogeneous (mottled internal enhancement) than the surrounding, darker liver. The aorta in front of the vertebral body is very bright and the spleen is strongly and unevenly enhanced. Panel B, labelled B at upper left: same level; the mass now appears darker (low attenuation) than the enhancing liver, with a thin slightly brighter peripheral rim, and the aorta is less bright than in A. No arrows, measurements, scale bar, window values or phase labels are printed.

panels.general_description: Axial CT of the upper abdomen showing a rounded, brighter heterogeneous mass in the posterior right hepatic lobe with a very bright aorta and strongly enhanced spleen.
panels.detailed_description: Liver on image left, spleen on image right. In the posterior right lobe near the lateral liver edge there is a rounded lesion whose interior is brighter than the neighbouring liver and mottled in texture. The aorta, round and bright anterior-left of the vertebral body, and the spleen (uneven bright enhancement) indicate an early contrast phase. Ribs, vertebra, stomach and the anterior abdominal wall are visible. The lesion edge is fairly well circumscribed. No printed size, arrow or phase label.

limitations: Identity and size of the treated mass are not otherwise delineated; no scale is printed.
Single small JPEG (about 770 px wide) of lossy quality; fine details such as tiny calcifications, residual nodules and vessel identity cannot be fully verified.
Orientation and contrast phase are not printed on the images; phase and sequence names come from the captions.
No arrows, scale bars or measurements are printed on the image.
